about: The zone's endless open ground (Dom 2026-10-27: one open world, the hero roams like an MMO). The page drew a 400-unit floor (data/stage.json ground.size) scaled with the start area (world.pitScale in data/respawn.json) and fixed on it, so it ended about 130 m out and its grid 26 m out. In the zone the same floor (same material, colour and fog, no texture) is made wide and FOLLOWS the hero: groundFollow.on moves the floor, its grid and the sun (so the shadow frustum stays on him) to the hero each frame, snapped to snapMetres, rounded up to a whole number of the stage's grid cells so the grid lines and the sand stay fixed in the world while he runs (no swim, no seam). groundRadiusMetres: metres of floor on every side of that point. gridRadiusMetres: how far the same grid is laid around it; beyond it the plain floor (a grid hundreds of lines deep only shimmers on a phone). edgeVisibility: the share of the floor's colour the fog may still show at the floor's edge (FogExp2, data/stage.json duel.fogDensity). cameraOffsetMetres: how far the camera may stand from the hero; the nearest the edge can be to the camera is groundRadiusMetres less this, and the fog must be down to edgeVisibility by then (the walking camera is 7.5 m behind him, data/respawn.json postKill.cameraMetres adds 8 m, the lock camera is nearer), so the edge is fog, not a line. cameraFarMetres: the zone camera's far plane (it was 180 m), at least that fog distance. With groundFollow.on false the floor stays where it was and groundRadiusMetres must also clear the walking reach (postKill.walkRadiusMetres + cameraMetres). Nothing in the open ground is drawn as an edge: this stage draws no wall, rim or ring (src/arena-stage.ts: the floor and the sky; the 'boundary' ring is hidden below full size, src/fight/scene.ts). ?ground=v1 = the old floor exactly as before (?postkill=v1 builds no zone, so also unchanged). The page keeps drawing in the sim's own coordinates (doubles in the sim, matrices in doubles on the CPU): only the ground and the sun are re-centred on the hero.

floorDepthPush.about: Sand quality (Dom 2026-10-27: 'glassy, wavy bands'). The grid lies on the floor in the same plane. Out past a few tens of metres the depth buffer cannot tell the two apart (the far plane is 420 m), so the floor and the grid lines fought for each pixel and drew wavy, scalloped rings over the distance. The floor has no texture and no reflection in play (flat colour, roughness 1): nothing else was wrong. This pushes the floor's depth back a hair (three.js polygonOffset, measured in the depth buffer's own steps, so the push grows with distance) so the grid always wins: the floor's colour, lighting and fog are untouched. Zone only (drawOpenGround); ?sand=v1 = the zone's floor without the push; ?ground=v1 and ?postkill=v1 never build it.
